title: Sprinkle Satellite
brief: Original kawaii future bass instrumental: bright major-key chords that pump under the kick, a light, bouncy half-time drop with a high pluck hook, a small vox patch singing the verse, music box and glockenspiel sparkle. 160 BPM, A major lifting to B major for the last drop. About 2:25.

sections.intent: Music box states the hook over a low-passed pad that opens; shaker enters at bar 5; no kick or bass
The vox sings a calmer verse tune; pluck chords, soft sub, kick and rim; hats and glock answers join for the second eight
Kick and bass out; pluck chords in eighths under a rising high-pass, the hook cell fragmented and accelerating, snare roll doubling in rate, riser; one beat and a half of silence before the drop
First high point: pumping supersaw chords, the full hook on the pluck lead, 808, half-time drums; phrase A ends on a half cadence, phrase B on the tonic
Contrast: no drums, piano broken chords and pad from the relative minor, the hook in augmentation on music box; from bar 57 the lead hints at the hook through an opening filter, claps and sub return
Pivot E (V of A = IV of B) into B major; the build routine again with a faster roll (sixteenth triplets, thirty-seconds)

Planned high point: the drop a whole step higher, the vox doubling the lead, pad and off-beat plucks added, sixteenth hats and a full-tempo clap; the melody peaks on F#6, the highest note of the piece
The groove thins and stops; music box hook and piano close on B add9, which rings out

tracks.name: Vox patch (pickups, drop answers and doubles)

decisions: Drops open on IV (D, then E in B major), not on the tonic, after a build that ends on V: a deceptive arrival. Phrase A of each drop closes on a 4-3 suspension over V (half cadence), phrase B on IV-V-I (perfect authentic cadence, 1 in the melody).
Colour chords: C#7 (V/vi) and the borrowed bVI (Fmaj7) between F#m7 and E give the drop a chromatic bass F#-F-E; the breakdown starts on the relative minor F#m9.
Key lift A -> B at bar 65 through a pivot: the breakdown ends on E (V of A), the build reads the same root as IV of B; F# major (with A#) confirms the new key.

Sounds start from Surge XT patches (pluck lead, vox patch, music box, chords, plucks, pad, sub); the 808 and the noise transitions stay on built-in presets (glide and sweeps), the kit on drum_synth, piano and glockenspiel on sampled banks.
Layers held back for drop 2: the vox doubling, the pad, the off-beat plucks, sixteenth hats and the thin full-tempo clap; drop 1 keeps the vox to short answers in the lead's gaps.

808 slides: the last 808 note of drop bars 6 and 14 overlaps the next downbeat, so the mono built-in 808 glides into the new root (the reason to keep the built-in preset after hearing it against two Surge 808s).

The future-bass wobble: the held chords at the end of each drop phrase bend 20 cents up and down in eighths (performance.bend on the chord part); the rest of the chords pump in a two-bar syncopated pattern under 10 dB of kick ducking.

Round 3: the plucks patch does not turn velocity into level and the part is levelled as a whole, so the velocity cuts of round 2 changed nothing; section levels now come from automation: -3 dB under the verse vox, -5 dB in the builds.

Round 2: the builds measured as loud as the drops (-8.9 vs -8.95 LUFS), carried by the plucks and the snare roll; the roll now rises from velocity 40 to 96, the build plucks and hats are softer, the riser 3 dB lower, so the drops arrive louder than what precedes them.

Build tension (Solberg 2014): kick and bass out, a high-pass on the plucks rising to 1.4-1.6 kHz, a snare roll doubling in rate, a six-bar noise riser and a reverse cymbal ending on the drop downbeat, one and a half beats of near silence with a three-note pickup; kick, 808, crash and impact return together on the downbeat.

musiclib.expression adds small timing deviation that keeps to the beat and a slow dynamics drift; the grid stays straight (no swing), kick and 808 kept tight, chord spread kept to a few ms as synth chords are struck by a sequencer.
authorship: Every note written by compose.py (this folder); performance deviation from musiclib.expression.
